hero.headline: JetBlue cuts Vero Beach to JFK route permanently after demand falls short
hero.body:
JetBlue is permanently ending flights from Vero Beach Regional Airport to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport starting Wednesday, September 9, less than a year after the airline began service. The airline said in a July statement obtained by CBS12 that demand for the route has not materialized as the company had hoped. The airport had completed about $5 million in construction projects for baggage claim and covered walkways in anticipation of the service.

JetBlue announced in December 2025 that it would begin serving Vero Beach Regional Airport with daily flights to JFK and Boston Logan International Airport. The airport expected the new service to bring an influx of passengers, prompting the improvements.

The airline will continue to serve Vero Beach through Boston. JetBlue said customers who booked flights on the discontinued route were notified directly and were issued a refund to their original form of payment.

The route cut comes as JetBlue adds eight new nonstop routes to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport.

hero.headline: 85-acre entertainment district in Tradition will bring 25 restaurants to Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
A nearly 85-acre entertainment district is planned along Village Parkway in the Tradition community, with developers saying construction on the first parcel could begin within six months. The Tradition Entertainment District would bring around 25 new restaurants and additional stores to Port St. Lucie.

Gustavo Lumer, CEO of Lumer Real Estate, is behind the property. The development is divided between four parcels along Village Parkway from Innovation Way to Hegener Drive.

Development will start on a 5.5-acre parcel off Innovation Way, which will include 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space. Lumer said 60 percent of that space is already leased, and he expects construction to start within six months.

"The retailers are eager to open yesterday. If we could pop it up next week and have it there, they're ready to go," Lumer said.

The next phase will develop two parcels totaling around 60 acres farther south, near the new Stars and Stripes Park. Lumer said this section would be the hub of the entertainment district. Plans include potentially 15 restaurants, a luxury gym, grocery stores, retail and possibly a movie theater.

"It'll be a place where you can park or come with your golf cart and spend the afternoon going around different places," Lumer said.

Lumer said the district will help keep and attract business in Port St. Lucie.

"The more brands that they keep opening, everybody's realizing, well, I'm the only one missing out, and so you'll see a lot of beautiful brands coming in a short, short time," Lumer said.

Neighbors in the area said they welcome the development. LaVaughn Harvey said he would visit often. Neighbor Tina Gramata said the district fills a community need.

"We need more places for people to go on a regular basis to intermingle," Gramata said.

Lumer said they are still working on final site approvals for the first parcel off Innovation Way and will begin working on site plan approval for the remaining three sites.

"That's a lot of retail and a lot of restaurants, and hopefully we can bring entertainment venues," Lumer said.

cards.headline: Man shoots dog in Fort Pierce after aggressive attack on family
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office confirmed a man shot one of two aggressive dogs in Indian River Estates after the animals attacked family members and prevented his wife from leaving her vehicle.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office confirmed Monday that a man shot one of two dogs that were behaving aggressively and attacking family members Sunday in the 5900 block of Palm Drive in the Indian River Estates subdivision in Fort Pierce.

Detectives with the Criminal Investigations Division reviewed surveillance footage and conducted interviews after the incident. According to the agency, the man's wife pulled into her driveway and two dogs approached her vehicle and prevented her from safely getting out. She contacted her husband for assistance.

The husband came outside and observed the dogs before returning inside the residence to retrieve a handgun, the sheriff's office said. When he came back outside, one dog charged toward him in an aggressive manner. As the dog approached and before he was bitten, the man fired his handgun, striking one of the dogs.

Both dogs fled to a nearby residence on Myrtle Drive, where they live. The owner took the injured dog to an emergency animal hospital for treatment, and the dog needed surgery. The agency said the status of the dog is unknown. The sheriff's office submitted a request to Animal Control for follow-up investigation.

"Investigators confirmed that two dogs were behaving aggressively and attempting to attack family members," the agency posted on Facebook. The man's wife pulled into her driveway, and two dogs approached her vehicle and prevented her from safely getting out of her vehicle. She contacted her husband for assistance. He said he came outside and observed the dogs before returning inside the residence to retrieve a handgun. When he came back outside, one dog charged toward him in an aggressive manner, the sheriff's office said. hero.headline: Sheriff's Office confirms Fort Pierce man acted in self-defense in dog shooting
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office confirmed Monday that a man acted in justified self-defense when he shot a dog Sunday in Fort Pierce's Indian River Estates subdivision after two dogs trapped his wife in her vehicle and one charged at him.

Detectives with the Criminal Investigations Division reviewed available surveillance footage and conducted interviews following the incident in the 5900 block of Palm Drive. The investigation confirmed that two dogs were behaving aggressively and attempting to attack family members, the agency posted on Facebook.

The man's wife pulled into her driveway when two dogs approached her vehicle and prevented her from safely getting out. She contacted her husband for assistance. He came outside and observed the dogs before returning inside the residence to retrieve a handgun. When he came back outside, one dog charged toward him in an aggressive manner. As the dog approached and before he was bitten, the man fired his handgun, striking one of the dogs.

After the shooting, both dogs fled to a nearby residence on Myrtle Drive where they reside. The owner took the injured dog to an emergency animal hospital for treatment, and the dog needed surgery. The agency submitted a request to Animal Control for follow-up investigation.

hero.headline: One northbound lane reopens on Florida's Turnpike after fatal Fort Pierce crash
hero.body:
One northbound lane of Florida's Turnpike has reopened in St. Lucie County following a crash that killed a 66-year-old Miami man Sunday morning. Only the left northbound lane is open near mile marker 166 in the Fort Pierce area. Drivers should continue to expect delays as the remaining lanes are closed.

The crash was reported at approximately 8:15 a.m., according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The 66-year-old man was driving a 2027 Freightliner M2 box truck north in the outside lane when, for reasons still under investigation, the truck partially entered the outside paved shoulder. The truck then re-entered the travel lanes and overturned before hitting a guardrail along the outside shoulder. The truck came to rest on its roof.

The driver was pronounced dead at the scene at 9:43 a.m. His identity has not been released, but FHP said his next of kin has been notified.

A 31-year-old Miami man who was a passenger in the truck was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. He was listed in stable condition.

hero.headline: Florida's Turnpike lanes near Fort Pierce reopen after fatal box truck rollover kills Miami driver
hero.body:
Both northbound and southbound lanes of Florida's Turnpike at Okeechobee Road have reopened Monday following a fatal box truck crash that closed the roadway for hours near mile marker 166 in unincorporated St. Lucie County. A 66-year-old Miami man driving the truck was pronounced dead at the scene at 9:43 a.m.

Witness Christopher Delerme told CBS12 that he and others were directly behind an Enterprise moving truck when they saw it begin swerving from left to right. Delerme said the truck suddenly swerved to the left and then back to the right before the driver lost control. He said the truck flipped twice on the Turnpike before hitting the guardrail, which brought the vehicle to a stop.

Florida Highway Patrol said the truck was traveling north in the outside lane when it partially entered the outside paved shoulder before re-entering the travel lanes and overturning. The truck then collided with a guardrail on the outside shoulder and came to rest on its roof. A 31-year-old Miami man who was also inside the truck was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce and is listed in stable condition.

Delerme and another passenger in the car, Stacey Delgado, said they immediately got out of their vehicle and called 911. When they approached the truck, it was upside down. They saw one unresponsive male and one female who was conscious and responsive inside the vehicle. The woman later confirmed there were only two people in the truck. According to Delerme, the woman was speaking Spanish and saying that a part of her body was hurting. Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the circumstances surrounding the crash. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office assisted with traffic control. The cause of the crash has not yet been determined.

hero.headline: Vero Beach quarterback Champ Monds done for season after medical procedure
hero.body:
Vero Beach High School star quarterback Champ Monds announced Saturday on Instagram that he has played his final game for the Fighting Indians after an unexpected medical procedure ended his senior season.

Monds wrote that his 2026 season has been cut short due to an unexpected minor procedure that needs to be addressed. The four-star quarterback and Notre Dame commit is just 16 years old. He reclassified to the 2027 recruiting class after being rated as the top quarterback in the country for 2028.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man shoots dog during confrontation in Indian River Estates, sheriff's office investigating
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is investigating after a man shot a dog Sunday in the Indian River Estates subdivision in Fort Pierce, saying the animal charged at him after preventing his wife from exiting her vehicle. The shooting occurred in the 5900 block of Palm Drive. Investigators are reviewing surveillance footage and conducting interviews with independent witnesses.

According to a preliminary investigation, the woman pulled into her driveway and two dogs approached her vehicle and prevented her from safely getting out. She contacted her husband for assistance. He said he came outside and observed the dogs before returning inside the residence to retrieve a handgun.

When he came back outside, one dog charged toward him in an aggressive manner, the sheriff's office said. As the dog approached and before he was bitten, the man fired his handgun, striking one of the dogs.

After the shooting, both dogs fled to a nearby residence on Myrtle Drive, where they reside. The owner transported the injured dog to an emergency animal hospital for treatment. The sheriff's office said the investigation remains active and no further conclusions will be drawn until all available evidence has been reviewed. The office remains committed to conducting a thorough and objective investigation and will provide additional verified information when appropriate.

cards.body:
Fort Pierce police are searching for three masked suspects after a man died from multiple gunshot wounds following a street altercation in September. Officers located the victim suffering from multiple gunshot wounds and transported him to a local hospital, where he later died.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting.

A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene. Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

hero.headline: Indiantown interim village manager Michael Giardino vows transparency in first public comments since appointment
hero.body:
Indiantown interim village manager Michael Giardino outlined his transparency-focused management approach in his first public comments since the Village Council appointed him Tuesday, one week after he was fired as Stuart city manager. Giardino replaced former Village Manager Taryn Kryzda, whom the council voted to terminate with some members citing no confidence during a meeting packed with residents urging more transparency about data center plans.

"Transparency is the Hallmark of governance," Giardino said. "I do things ethically, morally, and in accordance with the law and I believe this council wants to do the same and they heard their constituents loud and clear and so that's the way we'll move forward."

Giardino said council members reached out to him following his departure from Stuart. "I was invited to come by a few of the council members. They knew my circumstance and they were curious and interested, so I was there and I answered their calls," Giardino said. "Being received here in Indiantown, it's a joy and could have been destiny all along." The Navy veteran pointed to his experience running commercial airports as evidence he is prepared for the position, saying it is similar to running a small city with the same budgeting and personnel matters.

Residents said the change was welcome after three new council members were elected following the ouster of incumbents in the last election. "It was a step in the right direction because the previous council had lost the trust of the people," resident Kimberly Jackson Brown said. Resident Eric Miller said the outcome should be applauded because council members made the moves for the right reasons, acting as good Americans in elected roles.

Jackson Brown made clear that accountability will be expected from Giardino. "He needs to know that if he doesn't take instruction from the council as council takes instruction from the people then he can go to," Jackson Brown said.

hero.headline: Vero Beach mother held without bond on sexual battery charges after Michigan cybertip leads deputies to her home
hero.body:
A Vero Beach woman is being held without bond on two sexual battery charges after an Internet Crimes Against Children investigation in Michigan led deputies to her Indian River County home. Lisette Zamarripa, 28, was arrested Sept. 3 by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. She is charged with two counts of sexual battery and one count of electronic transmission of child sexual abuse material. Prosecutors intend to seek a grand jury indictment on two counts of capital sexual battery because of the children's ages.

Michigan State Police received a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children cybertip involving alleged child sexual abuse material associated with a Kik account, according to an arrest affidavit. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the account and found images and videos allegedly showing an adult woman engaging in sexual acts with two children, a 1-year-old girl and a 2-year-old boy, both her biological children. Michigan investigators identified the woman as Zamarripa after comparing material from the account with her Facebook profile. DCF took custody of the children.

Indian River County deputies went to Zamarripa's Vero Beach home after investigators believed the children could be in immediate danger. A family member confirmed Zamarripa was inside with her two children. Deputies said Zamarripa came outside with the children and was separated from them. After being advised of her rights, she allegedly admitted that she committed sexual acts involving both children during a FaceTime call with their biological father, who lives in Michigan. The affidavit says Zamarripa told detectives the acts had been discussed with the father beforehand and that she livestreamed at least one incident for him to view.

Michigan investigators also served a search warrant on Zamarripa's boyfriend, Kenneth Conkle, where he admitted to directing and recording the abuse. He confessed to separately abusing his own 1-year-old daughter. The biological father faces charges in Michigan including child sexual battery, four counts of production of aggravated child sexual abuse material, and five counts of using a computer to commit a crime. Florida charges against Conkle are pending. Deputies seized Zamarripa's cellphone, which she allegedly said was used to record the material. She is being held with no bond on the two sexual battery charges. Bond was set at $500,000, cash or surety, on the electronic transmission charge. Zamarripa's arraignment is scheduled for 9 a.m.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High cleared after bomb threat prompts evacuation, sheriff warns of false alarm costs
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. Friday following comprehensive sweeps of Fort Pierce Central High School after a bomb threat prompted an evacuation. No devices were located, and the scene has been deemed safe, deputies said. The area around Fort Pierce Central High School was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation, the sheriff's office said. St. Lucie County Public Schools notified parents of the threat. A second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned. During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were also asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous," she said. "I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up." Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously, but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that." The sheriff's warning underscored the seriousness with which law enforcement treats such incidents, regardless of whether they turn out to be hoaxes, and the commitment to pursuing criminal charges against those responsible for making false threats.

cards.headline: Man dies after shooting in Fort Pierce; police search for three masked suspects
cards.teaser: A man died after being shot multiple times following a verbal altercation in Fort Pierce. Police are searching for three masked males who witnesses saw running from the scene.
cards.body:
A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce, and police are searching for three masked suspects who fled the scene. The shooting happened in September, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

Officers located a man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to a local hospital, where he later died.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting.

Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

hero.headline: New interim Indiantown village manager Michael Giardino vows transparency after council ousts Taryn Kryzda
hero.body:
Michael Giardino, Indiantown's new interim village manager, outlined his leadership approach Tuesday after the Village Council voted to terminate former Village Manager Taryn Kryzda amid resident demands for transparency. The appointment came one week after Giardino lost his job as Stuart city manager.

The council cited no confidence in Kryzda as residents packed the meeting urging more transparency about plans for data centers. Giardino said transparency is the hallmark of governance.

"I do things ethically, morally, and in accordance with the law and I believe this council wants to do the same and they heard their constituents loud and clear and so that's the way we'll move forward," Giardino said.

Three new council members were elected after ousting incumbents in the last election. Resident Kimberly Jackson Brown said the change in management was a step in the right direction because the previous council had lost the trust of the people.

Resident Eric Miller said the outcome is to be applauded because those people made some pretty big moves and did it for the right reasons, not out of spite. He said they did it because they are acting as good Americans in an elected role.

Giardino said his appointment came after council members reached out to him following his departure from Stuart. Council members knew his circumstance and were curious and interested, so he answered their calls.

"Being received here in Indiantown, it's a joy and could have been destiny all along," Giardino said.

The Navy veteran points to his experience running commercial airports as evidence he is prepared for the position. He said it is running a small city, and the budgeting, personnel matters, and things to concentrate on are just about the same.

Jackson Brown said residents are cautiously optimistic but made clear that accountability will be expected. She said Giardino needs to know that if he does not take instruction from the council as council takes instruction from the people then he can go too.

hero.headline: Indiantown's new interim village manager pledges transparency after council ousts predecessor
hero.body:
Indiantown's new interim village manager Michael Giardino said transparency will guide his leadership after the Village Council terminated former Village Manager Taryn Kryzda on Tuesday, with some council members citing no confidence. The move came as residents packed the council meeting urging more transparency about plans for data centers.

Giardino's appointment came one week after he lost his job as Stuart city manager. Council members reached out to him following his departure from Stuart. "I was invited to come by a few of the council members. They knew my circumstance and they were curious and interested, so I was there and I answered their calls," Giardino said. "Being received here in Indiantown, it's a joy and could have been destiny all along."

"Transparency is the Hallmark of governance," Giardino said. "I do things ethically, morally, and in accordance with the law and I believe this council wants to do the same and they heard their constituents loud and clear and so that's the way we'll move forward." The Navy veteran pointed to his experience running commercial airports as evidence he is prepared for the position. "It is running a small city. The budgeting is the same, the personnel matters are the same, the things that you concentrate on are just about the same," Giardino said.

Resident Kimberly Jackson Brown said the change in management was a step in the right direction. "The previous council had lost the trust of the people," Jackson Brown said. Three new council members were elected after ousting incumbents in the last election. Resident Eric Miller said the council members "did it for the right reasons, not out of spite—they did it because they're acting as good Americans in an elected role."

Jackson Brown warned that accountability will be expected from the new manager. "He needs to know that if he doesn't take instruction from the council as council takes instruction from the people then he can go to," Jackson Brown said.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School cleared after bomb threat; no devices found
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted a full evacuation and sweep of the campus. No devices were located, and the scene was deemed safe at around 3 p.m., deputies said.

The area around Fort Pierce Central High School was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation, the sheriff's office said. Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat and a second message confirmed the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. Jones said the timing made the situation even more unsettling. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous," she said. "I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were also asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School cleared after bomb threat prompts evacuation, sheriff warns false alarms drain resources
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted an evacuation and comprehensive sweep of the campus. No devices were located and the scene was deemed safe around 3 p.m., deputies said.

The area around Fort Pierce Central High School was secured and evacuated around 1 p.m. while the sheriff's office bomb team conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation. Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat and a second message was sent confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities resumed as planned.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous. I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were also asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911.

cards.headline: Four Fort Pierce officers credited with saving woman in crisis on South Causeway Bridge
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police officers talked down and physically pulled a woman from the outer railing of the South Causeway Bridge on Wednesday during a mental health crisis.
cards.body:
Four Fort Pierce police officers are being credited with saving a woman who was experiencing a mental health crisis on the South Causeway Bridge on Wednesday.

The woman was sitting on the outer railing of the bridge facing the water when officers arrived, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department. Two officers took the initiative to keep her focused while assessing the situation. The other two officers then pulled her from the railing and back to safety when immediate action became necessary.

All four officers worked together to protect the woman from further harm and ensure she received appropriate care, the department said.

The Fort Pierce Police Department praised the officers in a Facebook post, saying their teamwork, compassion, and decisive action directly saved a life and exemplified their commitment to protecting the community.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School evacuated, swept, and cleared after bomb threat
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team cleared Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted evacuation and a comprehensive sweep of the campus. The school was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. No devices were located, and deputies gave the all clear at around 3 p.m.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous. I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, was inside when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said. Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat, and a second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that." During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel.

cards.headline: Three masked suspects sought after fatal shooting in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A man died after being shot multiple times following a verbal altercation in Fort Pierce. Witnesses saw three masked males run from the scene.
cards.body:
A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce following a verbal altercation that escalated to gunfire. Three masked suspects fled on foot and remain unidentified.

The shooting happened in September. Fort Pierce police officers found the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to a local hospital, where he later died.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene. Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team cleared Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat forced an evacuation around 1 p.m. No devices were found.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. Friday following comprehensive sweeps of Fort Pierce Central High School after a bomb threat forced an evacuation. No devices were located, and the scene has been deemed safe, deputies said.

The area around Fort Pierce Central High School was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation, the sheriff's office said. Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat. A second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned, Martin said.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. Jones said the timing made the situation even more unsettling. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous," she said. "I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously, but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."
